questions.answer: 1200 J. The lift does 200 N x 6 m = 1200 J against gravity; the sideways move does no work against gravity because the weight acts downwards, at right angles to the sideways movement, and the height does not change.
questions.explanation: Work against gravity depends only on the vertical rise: 200 x 6 = 1200 J. Moving horizontally at a constant height changes no GPE, so it adds nothing.

questions.prompt: A crane lifts a load weighing 200 N straight up by 6 m, then moves it sideways 4 m at the same height. Calculate the total work done against gravity, and explain the sideways part.
questions.workedSolution: Work against gravity = 200 x 6 = 1200 J for the lift; the sideways 4 m is at constant height, so it adds 0 J. Total = 1200 J.

questions.prompt: Two motors each do 600 J of work lifting identical loads. Motor A takes 12 s and motor B takes 20 s. Calculate the power of each motor, and state which is more powerful and by how much.
questions.workedSolution: A: 600 J / 12 s = 50 W. B: 600 J / 20 s = 30 W. A is more powerful, by 50 - 30 = 20 W.
